Title: Indo-Japan: Japan’s Key Agenda
Short_Summary: The article explores the evolving India–Japan strategic partnership, highlighting key areas of cooperation in trade, investment, semiconductors, technology and supply chain resilience. Indo-Japan: Japan’s Key Agenda

Syllabus areas:

GS Paper II – international relations

Japan Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi visited India in July 2026.

India as an indispensable partner of Japan did not mean that China was being given a short shrift or “dumped”; Indo-Pacific open and free, India was a reliable partner.

China is Japan’s largest trading partner with two-way trade of around $325 billion, predominantly of high-tech components, machines and consumer items.

On the other hand, India accounts for less than 2% of Japan’s total global trade.

Tokyo has been one of India’s top investors, spread over automobile, electronics, infra, logistics and finance. There are nearly 1,500 Japanese companies in India operating in a very different environment compared to the restrictive environment of the past.

Recent visit of Donald Trump to China.

India-Japan relationship has significantly matured. Over time, it has evolved from standard bilateral partnership to special strategic partnership and global partnership.

Japan has played a significant role in supporting India’s priorities such as energy, transportation and environment.

A key area for progress is the renegotiation of Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

CEPA - Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA): A bilateral agreement between countries that promotes trade and economic cooperation by reducing tariffs and non-tariff barriers, facilitating investment, improving market access and strengthening collaboration in services, technology and other sectors.

Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) represents key areas for future Indo-Japan ties:

  • Semiconductors represent key areas for future Indo-Japan ties.
  • Supply chain resilience.
  • India’s strength in digital infrastructure and electronics manufacturing complements Japan’s expertise.
  • Technology and Artificial Intelligence: Robotics, cybersecurity and advanced digital solutions.
  • Empowering youth is critical: Increased collaboration between universities, industries and research institutions.
  • Indo-Pacific region emerged as the centre of global economic and strategic activities.
